title: Silas and the Gravity
premise: Ines Brightwater, a clone of a murdered detective, has spent seven years hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding from the war between Earth and the Belt. When gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, Ines realizes it was a signal — and that the message hidden inside it was encoded by his original before dying. Hunted by both fleets, Ines must carry the truth of who really started the war to the one place both sides fear: the neutral archive at Ceres. He delivers it, exposing Earth's own admiralty as the architects of the conflict, but chooses to broadcast it openly rather than trade it for his freedom — ending the war and, with it, any hope of staying invisible.
about_author: Isandro Galloway is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about people who are very good at their jobs and very bad at staying out of trouble.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Ines Brightwater's POV. Hauling ore through contested orbits, Ines feels gravity die for exactly nine seconds — everywhere, all at once. His ship's logs record an impossible data pulse riding the fluctuation. The emotional beat is dread: after seven years of careful invisibility, something enormous just noticed everyone, including him.

chapters.title: The Original's Ghost
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Decoding fragments of the pulse, Ines finds metadata signed with his own genetic donor's case number — the murder he inherited but never solved. A Belt contact warns him both fleets have flagged the anomaly. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance, as the dead man's work pulls him back into a life he cloned himself to escape.

chapters.title: Cargo Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Mara Voss, an Earth naval intelligence officer ordered to retrieve 'a Brightwater asset.' She boards Ines's ship under inspection pretense and finds the decoded fragment. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; two professionals lying fluently while each recognizes the other is doing the same.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The fragment reveals his original discovered Earth's admiralty manufactured the first Belt attack to justify fleet expansion — and was killed for it. The nine-second flicker was a dead-man's-switch broadcast of the evidence. Emotional beat: fury and vertigo as Ines realizes justice outside the law is now his only option.

chapters.title: The Long Way to Ceres
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Ordered to capture or kill Ines, Mara instead feeds his pursuers false coordinates, unable to explain even to herself why. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against truth — she serves Earth, but not the men who murdered a detective to protect a lie.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Tycho Drift
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Belt militia captures Ines, believing he carries an Earth weapon. He must convince zealots that the evidence exonerates the Belt too — that both sides were played. Emotional beat: persuasion under threat, where telling the whole truth is the only thing that keeps him alive.

chapters.title: The Price of the Message
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Earth offers Ines immunity and a new identity in exchange for the evidence; the Belt offers him hero status if he releases only the half that damns Earth. Emotional beat: temptation on both sides — every offer is a way to survive by letting the corruption stand.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive Light
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Mara's superiors, learning of her deception, use her as bait to trap Ines at the Ceres archive. Confronted with what she's enabled, she turns her weapons on her own boarding team. Emotional beat: the cost of delayed conscience — loyalty finally breaking cleanly toward truth.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Wounded, cornered in the archive core as Earth's last transmission loop nears its end, Ines faces the choice: sell the evidence quietly or broadcast everything, including parts that shame the Belt and implicate his own original's compromises. He broadcasts all of it. Emotional beat: climax — power refused, truth chosen at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Gravity, Restored
chapters.summary: Epilogue-style dual POV. Fleets stand down amid scandal; admirals fall, wars end messily rather than neatly. Ines, no longer invisible, takes a slow hauler contract while Mara, court-martialed and freed, asks to come along. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — justice delivered imperfectly, and two people finally unburdened.
